verdict.rationale: Navan documents two built-in assistants. Ava analyzes and summarizes spend, compares it to policy and finds savings. Navan Edge lets users book flights, hotels and restaurants by chatting, and asks for explicit confirmation before booking, changing or canceling a trip. The delegation caveats are significant: Edge is reserved for the most frequent travelers and runs as a separate iOS/web experience, and the evidence also describes Edge as human travel agents, so it is unclear how much the AI handles. The MCP server connects external assistants and is not credited here. Missing for 10: confirmation that Edge's booking is AI-driven rather than human-agent-driven, availability of an assistant across the main product for all users, documented ability to delegate expense or approval actions (not just analysis), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: You can book flights, hotels, and restaurant reservations by chatting with Navan Edge.
Navan Edge will always ask for your explicit confirmation before booking, changing, or canceling any trip.
Ava slices and dices real-time spend data, provides insights into T&E questions, and proactively finds opportunities for savings.
Reserved for the world's most frequent travelers
